_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Inside Decoded, 160K views, 1 month old; AI/altered-content label). Frames every 0.5 s for the first 4 s then every 5-6 s; no sound probe (same channel as pBBBNOUxDh4). Shots approximate. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: close over Earth's surface from low orbit, the horizon curving, stars above; a short caption mid-frame
hook.firstLine: A satellite network can put internet almost anywhere on Earth

shots.picture: one continuous pull-back from Earth's surface out to the whole globe wrapped in a cloud of satellites
the globe turning inside its shell of tiny satellites
a framed flat world map card on black, countries coloured by status with a legend
a phone on a wooden table at home, a hand taps it, a lamp behind
the dish on a tiled roof, a thin beam rising from it
satellites in low orbit above Earth's edge
a ground station diorama: white radomes beside a server building, a beam coming in
diagram in 3D: house and ground station on floating tiles, beams up to two satellites
push in past a railing to the dish switching satellites
two satellites over cloud tops linked by a laser line
a countryside terrain tile with fields and villages, a cable path to the coast
a satellite drops a green beam straight into the terrain tile
the terrain tile with a ground station inside, a green beam to it
a switch cabinet next to a dish at the tile's edge
a framed map card of one country, then another, each with a callout tag
the globe again, countries coloured, under a subscribe card

lines.gist: the network can reach almost anywhere on Earth
yet dozens of countries still do not have it
a user taps, the signal goes from the phone to the dish
up to thousands of satellites, then down to a ground station
a round trip takes milliseconds; the dish keeps switching satellites
satellites can also pass data between themselves
that worries governments: the data can skip their cables
countries want a station inside the border; one company holds the switch
so it is not the tech holding it back, it is the rules

ending.cta: Subscribe card over the final globe
ending.lastFrame: the coloured globe from the opening under a subscribe card

whyItWorks: the first 2.5 s is one continuous camera move from the ground to the whole planet: motion, scale and subject at once
the paradox (reaches everywhere, yet banned) is set in the first two lines
each step of the signal's path is its own small diorama, so the route is followed shot by shot
it ends on the globe it opened on, so the replay starts on the same picture
